title: Cancer Care + Sickle Cell: Neutropenia, Low Platelets, Crisis

questions.stem: A client on chemotherapy has a neutrophil count of 400 and a temperature of 38.4 but says they feel fine. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Recheck the temperature in four hours
Treat it as urgent: cultures, then the first antibiotic within one hour
Document it, since the client feels fine

questions.explanation: B is correct: this is neutropenic fever, an emergency, even though they feel fine. A, C, and D delay treatment while sepsis can develop within hours.

questions.stem: What absolute neutrophil count is severe?
questions.explanation: C is correct: below 1,500 is low, and below 500 is severe. B is the cutoff for low, not severe. A and D are not the cutoffs taught.

questions.stem: Why might a fever be the only sign of infection in a client with very few neutrophils?

options.text: With almost no neutrophils, there is little pus or redness

questions.explanation: B is correct: with almost no neutrophils, there's little pus or redness, so a fever may be the only sign of a deadly infection. A, C, and D are not what the video teaches.

options.text: A single 38.3, or 38.0 lasting over an hour
Only a temperature of 39 or higher

questions.explanation: B is correct: a single 38.3, or 38.0 lasting over an hour. A is below the cutoff. C waits too long. D is too short for the 38.0 rule.

questions.stem: Which are common precautions for a client with low white cells? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: clean hands, a private room, no sick visitors, and no rectal temperatures or suppositories, per your facility. E is exactly what to avoid.

questions.stem: A client has low platelets. Which actions fit bleeding precautions? Select all that apply.

options.text: Give medicines as shots into the muscle

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: soft toothbrush, electric razor, hold pressure on punctures, and prevent falls and straining. E and F are avoided with low platelets.

questions.stem: A client in sickle cell crisis arrives at the emergency department in severe pain. When should pain medicine be given?

options.text: Only if the pain lasts more than four hours

questions.explanation: A is correct: give pain medicine within one hour of arrival, and reassess every 30 to 60 minutes. B, C, and D undertreat pain, a classic danger.

questions.stem: Which action is correct during a sickle cell crisis?

options.text: Apply cold packs to painful joints
Keep the client warm and use the incentive spirometer

questions.explanation: B is correct: keep the client warm, never cold packs, and use the incentive spirometer. A: cold makes sickling worse. C: avoid meperidine. D: give fluids, without overloading.

questions.stem: A client in sickle cell crisis has sudden chest pain, a temperature of 38.5, and an oxygen saturation of 91%. What is the priority?

options.text: Give oxygen and notify the provider now
Put cold packs on the chest
Walk in the hall to open the lungs

questions.explanation: A is correct: chest pain, fever, and low oxygen mean possible acute chest syndrome, an emergency. B: cold makes sickling worse. C and D delay care.

questions.stem: For a client in sickle cell crisis, when should oxygen be given?

options.text: Never; it hides acute chest syndrome

questions.explanation: B is correct: give oxygen if the saturation is below 95%. A waits too long. C and D are not what the video teaches.
